name: rigby2d
description: Let Claude open, rig, animate, check and convert your Rigby2D 2D animation projects.
long_description: Connects Claude to your Rigby2D projects (.rigby work files and skeleton .json / .skel exports). Ask Claude to explain a rig, find missing images, add bones and animations, set eased keys, rig a layered PSD with AutoRig, reuse animations on other characters, set up film output, poses, face controls and lip-sync, or run Python scripts. Claude only reads and writes files inside the project folders you choose here.

tools.name: inspect_project
tools.description: Summarize a Rigby2D project file: format and version, counts of bones, slots, skins, constraints, events and images, the animations with their durations, and any read warnings.

tools.name: describe_rig
tools.description: List the bone hierarchy with setup-pose transforms (Y up, degrees), the slots in draw order with their attachments, and the attachments of each extra skin.

tools.name: describe_animation
tools.description: Show one animation: its duration, the key times of every bone, slot, deform, IK and draw-order timeline, its events, and other timelines it holds.

tools.name: sample_pose
tools.description: Evaluate the skeleton with the Rigby2D runtime: the setup pose, or an animation at a time.

tools.name: validate_project
tools.description: Check a project for problems: structure, images missing from its work file, atlas or images folder, animations without keys, whether skeleton JSON 4.3 round-trips the data exactly, and whether binary .skel export is possible.

tools.name: convert_project
tools.description: Write a project as skeleton JSON (format 3.8, 4.2 or 4.3) or binary .skel (4.3).

tools.name: export_defold_model
tools.description: Write a Rigby2D model for Defold from a character (.rigby work file, or .skel / .json with its atlas or images): the skeleton (<name>.rigbyskel), its images unpacked into images/ with a Defold atlas (<name>.atlas), the component (<name>.rigbymodel) and a game object holding it (<name>.go).

tools.name: export_sprite_sheet
tools.description: Render animations frame by frame into a sprite sheet for engines that play frames: 'json' writes <name>.png and <name>.json (a JSON hash as TexturePacker writes it, read by Phaser, PixiJS and others, with Aseprite frameTags, durations and a pivot at the skeleton's origin); 'defold' writes <name>/<animation>_<n>.png frames and <name>.atlas; 'frames' writes the frames only.

tools.name: add_bone
tools.description: Add a bone as a child of an existing bone, with its setup pose relative to the parent (x, y, rotation in degrees, length).

tools.name: set_bone_setup
tools.description: Change a bone's setup (rest) pose relative to its parent: x, y, rotation, scaleX, scaleY, shearX, shearY (degrees for angles) and length.

tools.name: add_animation
tools.description: Add an empty animation.

tools.name: set_bone_key
tools.description: Set a key on a bone in an animation (replacing a key at the same time).

tools.name: delete_bone_key
tools.description: Delete the key of a bone channel at a time in an animation.

tools.name: set_attachment_key
tools.description: Show an attachment in a slot from a time on in an animation (an image swap), or hide the slot's attachment with hide: true.

tools.name: set_event_key
tools.description: Fire an event at a time in an animation (games receive it during playback).

tools.name: batch_edit
tools.description: Apply many edits in one call, loading and saving the project once, atomically: all of them are saved, or none.

tools.name: set_workspace
tools.description: Set the project's workspace: 'game' (for game engines; skeleton exports) or 'film' (for film and video: output settings, renders, face controls, audio).

tools.name: set_output
tools.description: Set the film output: frame rate (presets: 12, 15, 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 48, 50, 60; any rate up to 240), size in pixels, background ('transparent' or a #rrggbb color), and framing: 'auto' (fit the animation), 'fixed' (center frame_x, frame_y and frame_scale world units per pixel), or 'camera' (follow a bone named 'camera', created if missing).

tools.name: save_pose
tools.description: Save a pose to the pose library: the local transforms of the given bones (default: every bone) and the attachments their slots show (mouth shapes, eyes).

tools.name: apply_pose
tools.description: Apply a saved pose at an amount (0 to 1; image swaps switch at 0.5).

tools.name: delete_pose
tools.description: Delete a pose from the pose library.

tools.name: add_face_control
tools.description: Add a face control: a slider from 0 to 1 that blends from one pose ('from', default the setup pose) to another ('to'), such as brows up, eyes closed or mouth open.

tools.name: set_face_control
tools.description: Set a face control to a value (0 to 1).

tools.name: delete_face_control
tools.description: Delete a face control (its poses stay in the library).

tools.name: add_audio_track
tools.description: Add a sound file (.wav, .mp3, .ogg, .m4a, .aac, .flac) as an audio track of an animation, starting at 'offset' seconds.

tools.name: set_audio_track
tools.description: Change an audio track's start time (offset, seconds) or volume.

tools.name: remove_audio_track
tools.description: Remove an audio track from an animation.

tools.name: lip_sync
tools.description: Lip-sync an animation to one of its audio tracks.

tools.name: rename_bone
tools.description: Rename a bone.

tools.name: rename_animation
tools.description: Rename an animation.

tools.name: delete_animation
tools.description: Delete an animation and its audio tracks.

tools.name: set_slot
tools.description: Change a slot's setup: the attachment it shows (or hide: true to show none) and its color (#rrggbb or #rrggbbaa).

tools.name: detect_parts
tools.description: Preview Rigby AutoRig on layered artwork: which body part each layer is (head, torso, upperarm, forearm, hand, arm, thigh, shin, foot, leg, eye, mouth, hair, tail, ...), its side and whether that came from the layer name or its position.

tools.name: autorig
tools.description: Rigby AutoRig: rig layered artwork in one step.

tools.name: map_bones
tools.description: Preview how retarget_animation matches the bones of a source character to a target character: by name, similar name ("L_Arm" and "arm.l"), body part ("UpperArm_Left" and "upperarm_l") or your mapping.

tools.name: retarget_animation
tools.description: Copy animations from one character to another (any format): bones are matched automatically (see map_bones; override with mapping), movement is scaled to the target's size (scale 'auto') and rotated into its bones' frames, curves are kept, and slot, event and IK keys follow by name.

tools.name: add_actor
tools.description: Put a character (another .rigby work file) into this scene as an actor.

tools.name: add_clip
tools.description: Place a clip of an actor's animation on a shot of the scene, NLE-style: from 'start' it plays the animation between 'in' and 'out' at 'speed', 'loops' times, crossfading from the actor's previous clip over 'blend' seconds; after it ends the actor holds the last frame until its next clip.

tools.name: remove_clip
tools.description: Remove an actor's clip that starts at 'start' (seconds) on a shot.

tools.name: set_actor
tools.description: Change an actor: its setup position, size, facing, skin or name.

tools.name: set_layer_depth
tools.description: Set the depth of a top-level stage bone (a background or foreground layer) for parallax: when the 'camera' bone moves, a layer at depth z keeps up with focal / (focal + z) of the motion (focal 1000 by default), keeping its drawn size.

tools.name: run_script
tools.description: Run a Python script against a project with the Rigby2D scripting API (`import rigby`: bones, slots, animations, keys, selection, time; see https://rigby2d.com/docs/scripting.html), then save the project.

project_folders.title: Project folders
project_folders.description: The folders with your Rigby2D projects. Claude can only open and change files inside them.
